name: Ringo Corponation DriftPack RV-6 Personal Vectored Thrust Harness
product_name: Ringo Corponation DriftPack RV-6 Personal Vectored Thrust Harness
description:
The DriftPack RV-6 is a wearable, short-range personal aerial mobility harness manufactured by Ringo Corponation, designed for individual transit across GLMZ's mid-to-upper vertical strata where conventional transit infrastructure is sparse or inaccessible. The harness consists of four articulated micro-turbine pods mounted on a carbon-ceramic spine frame worn across the torso and shoulders, fed by a dual CascadeCell supercapacitor bank integrated into the lower back section. At full charge, the RV-6 provides approximately 18 minutes of sustained flight at a maximum altitude of 340 meters above ground level, with a top horizontal speed of 95 km/h. The thrust vector control system interfaces directly with the wearer's center-of-gravity through a gyroscopic feedback harness, allowing experienced operators to fly with minimal manual input, though Ringo markets a neural control module upgrade compatible with their EchoLimb proprioceptive interface platform for users with upper-limb augmentation.

The RV-6 is legally restricted to licensed operators in designated aerial corridors managed by Tessera Corponation's airspace authority, but the black market for unlicensed units has made it one of the most prevalent illegal mobility tools in GLMZ's upper slum strata. Ringo deliberately engineered the DriftPack with modular components that are individually legal to purchase, a design philosophy that has created a thriving gray-market assembly ecosystem. The harness includes an emergency ballistic parachute deployment system rated to 40 meters minimum altitude, a feature that has become tragically relevant given the frequency of unlicensed use in sub-40-meter inter-building gaps.

Among licensed corporate courier services, the RV-6 is the standard-issue personal transport for Tier 2 rapid-response logistics personnel. Among Tier 4 populations, a working DriftPack assembled from salvage components — known as a 'ghost rig' — represents months of savings and the difference between economic mobility and confinement to a flooded lower district.
base_technologies: Ouroboros Energy CascadeCell Mk.IV Supercapacitor Array
Ringo Corponation EchoLimb PR-9 Proprioceptive Feedback Prosthetic Interface
social_impact: The DriftPack RV-6 has created a sharp and politically charged divide in GLMZ between those who can afford licensed aerial mobility and those who risk death assembling gray-market equivalents. Tessera's airspace enforcement drones are programmed to fire suppression charges at unlicensed flyers in restricted corridors, a policy that has killed dozens of Tier 4 riders attempting to reach employment or medical facilities inaccessible by ground transit. Ringo Corponation has publicly condemned unlicensed assembly while quietly maintaining a parts distribution network that makes it trivially possible, a calculated business strategy that generates revenue from both the licensed market and the gray-market assembly ecosystem.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 teenager who built a ghost rig from salvage has accidentally drifted into a Tessera restricted airspace corridor and been detained — her rig contains components that shouldn't exist on the civilian market
A series of DriftPack failures in the same district have been traced to a single batch of counterfeit CascadeCell modules — someone is deliberately seeding the gray market with sabotaged components
A licensed corporate courier using an RV-6 witnesses something from altitude that they were never meant to see, and now Tessera's enforcement team is hunting them across the mid-city air corridors
Ringo Corponation is developing an RV-6 successor with mandatory real-time telemetry — the existing RV-6 user community, legal and illegal alike, is organizing to resist the update
